This keyhole-shaped tumulus is part of the {{ill|Suga-no-Sawa Kofun Cluster|ja|菅ノ沢古墳群|qid=Q140446106}}. It has not been Historic Site1 as a historic site.

== Overview ==
The tumulus was constructed on the southern slope of a branch hill of the Kanayama Hills in eastern Gunma Prefecture. It is situated at the northern end of the Suga-no-Sawa Kofun Cluster, with the {{ill|Suga-no-Sawa Gobyō Kofun|ja|菅ノ沢御廟古墳|qid=Q140446107}} located to the north{{Sfn|Imaizumiguchi Hachiman-yama Kofun (Su11lementary Kofun)|2002}}. The mound and the stone chamber have suffered significant destruction, but excavations were conducted in {{ill|1994|en|1994|qid=Q2067|lt=1994}} and {{ill|1995|en|1995|qid=Q2068|lt=1995}} (Heisei 6–7).

The tumulus has a well-developed front section facing west<ref>The "Jōmō Kofun Sōran" initially described the mound as having its front section facing east, but the Ota City Board of Education revised this in their investigation report to face west, placing the stone chamber in the rear circular section.</ref>. burial goods such as {{ill|Cylindrical haniwa|ja|円筒埴輪}} (including asagao-type haniwa) and {{ill|figurative haniwa|ja|形象埴輪}} (depictions of people, horses, houses, shields, etc.) have been unearthed, possibly sourced from the {{ill|Kita-Kanai Komagata Shrine Haniwa Kiln Group|ja|北金井駒形神社埴輪窯跡群}}{{Sfn|Imaizumiguchi Hachiman-yama Kofun (Su11lementary Kofun)|2002}}. Surrounding the mound, a moat 2.5 meters wide and 1 meter deep has been identified on the north side of the rear section{{Sfn|Imaizumiguchi Hachiman-yama Kofun (Su11lementary Kofun)|2002}}.

The burial facility is a {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|ko|굴식 돌방무덤|zh|橫穴式石室|qid=Q11543435}} located in the rear section, opening to the south. It measures 10 meters in total length and contains a {{ill|House-shaped Sarcophagus|ja|家形石棺|qid=Q17192769}}. Despite evidence of looting, burial goods recovered include earrings from within the sarcophagus and straight swords, short swords, handguards, iron arrowheads, cylindrical silver-bronze products, coil-shaped gold-bronze products, and {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|qid=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} from the chamber{{Sfn|Imaizumiguchi Hachiman-yama Kofun (Su11lementary Kofun)|2002}}. The tumulus is estimated to have been constructed in the late {{ill|6th century|af|6de eeu|als|6. == History ==
* Genbun 3 (1738): Documented in the "Nitta Kanayama Stone Sarcophagus Inquiry Report"{{Sfn|Imaizumiguchi Hachiman-yama Kofun (Su11lementary Kofun)|2002}}.
* {{ill|1938|en|1938|qid=Q18645|lt=1938}} (Shōwa 13): Listed as "Morita Village Mound No. 12" in the "Jōmō Kofun Sōran."
* {{ill|1994|en|1994|qid=Q2067|lt=1994}} and {{ill|1995|en|1995|qid=Q2068|lt=1995}}: Excavations conducted during retaining wall construction for landslide prevention measures on the southern side of the tumulus. Report published by the Ota City Board of Education in {{ill|1996|en|1996|qid=Q2070|lt=1996}}.

== Mound area ==
The area of the tumulus are as follows{{Sfn|Imaizumiguchi Hachiman-yama Kofun (Su11lementary Kofun)|2002}}:
* Total length: Estimated reconstruction at 60 meters
* Rear circular section diameter: Estimated reconstruction at 29 meters
* Front section width: Estimated reconstruction at 50 meters

== burial ==
[[File:Imaizumiguchi Hachiman-yama Kofun, sekishitsu.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Remaining Stone Chamber}}]]
The burial facility is a {{ill|Yokoana-style Stone Chamber|ja|横穴式石室|ko|굴식 돌방무덤|zh|橫穴式石室|qid=Q11543435}} constructed in the rear circular section, with an opening facing south. Its area are as follows{{Sfn|Imaizumiguchi Hachiman-yama Kofun (Su11lementary Kofun)|2002}}:
* burial chamber (gen-shitsu): 5.7 meters long, 2.2 meters wide, 2.4 meters high
* Passageway (sendo): 4.8 meters long, 1.3 meters wide

The chamber's construction materials include {{ill|Chart (disambiguation)|en|Chart (disambiguation)|qid=Q1067738|lt=Chert}} and Kanayama stone (welded tuff){{Sfn|Ota City History, General Edition: Prehistoric and Ancient|1996}}. Traces of white clay coating remain between the chamber's rear stones and ceiling stones{{Sfn|Imaizumiguchi Hachiman-yama Kofun (Su11lementary Kofun)|2002}}.

A house-shaped sarcophagus made of {{ill|Andesite|en|Andesite|qid=Q181908|lt=Andesite}} is located inside the chamber. The sarcophagus is oriented east-west, perpendicular to the chamber's main axis. Its area are{{Sfn|Imaizumiguchi Hachiman-yama Kofun (Su11lementary Kofun)|2002}}:
* Lid: 1.91 meters long, 1.05 meters wide, 0.45 meters high
* Body: 1.85 meters long, 0.97 meters wide, 0.54 meters high

The lid features two rope-loop projections on the passageway side{{Sfn|Imaizumiguchi Hachiman-yama Kofun (Su11lementary Kofun)|2002}}.

burial goods recovered include:
* From the sarcophagus: Two gold-bronze earrings
* From the burial chamber: Straight swords, short swords, handguards, iron arrowheads, and {{ill|Sue pottery|en|Sue pottery|qid=Q7634351|lt=Sue pottery}} (goblets and jars)
* From the passageway floor: Cylindrical silver-bronze products and coil-shaped gold-bronze products{{Sfn|Imaizumiguchi Hachiman-yama Kofun (Su11lementary Kofun)|2002}}.
